en: The *Bodhimaṇḍālaṃkāra-dhāraṇī-sūtra*. [Bestowed upon] the Kaifu Yitongsi,
Teci, Shih Hongluqing, Duke of Suku with a fief of three thousand households,
invested with purple robes, and posthumously honored as Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial.

Posthumously titled Dajian (Great Mirror), with the formal title Dayangzhi (Great Vast Wisdom), the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Monastery, respectfully translated by imperial decree: Thus have I heard.
At one time, the Bhagavat was dwelling in the vast and expansive Great Garden of the great city of Vārāṇasī.
He was accompanied by a community of five thousand bhikṣus,
all of whom were great arhats whose outflows were exhausted and who had accomplished what was to be done.
Having attained their own benefit and severed all fetters of existence,
there were also five hundred bodhisattva-mahāsattvas present with him. At that time,
on the fifteenth day of the full moon, the World-Honored One sat and preached the Dharma.
In that assembly were immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of sentient beings—
Brahmins, Kṣatriyas, brahmacāris, Nirgranthas, and others,

including various non-Buddhist practitioners of frivolous speculation and illusory arts, those who dwell in cemeteries, those who wear rags, those who observe the cow-vow, and those who dwell in mountain valleys observing ascetic precepts.
Furthermore, together with a great assembly of devas, they all sat before the Buddha in the gathered multitude.
At that time, the great assembly of those holding wrong views and followers of heterodox paths harbored doubts and difficulties in their minds.
The Tathāgata, out of compassion, comforted them all.
Let them ask whatever they wish.
Furthermore, there were devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and so forth.
They sat surrounding him on all sides.
Furthermore, Śakra, the Lord of Devas,
was present with a retinue of hundreds of thousands of devas from the Trāyastriṃśa heaven.
Surrounded by his retinue from before and behind, he came to where the Buddha was.
Furthermore, the Brahma King, together with a hundred thousand kinsmen of the Brahmakāyika devas who are lords of the Sahā world, all assembled there.
Furthermore, there were the Sun and Moon Devas, Ratnacandra, Pūrṇacandra, Deva Balavān, and others;

together with the hosts of great yakṣa generals, Maheśvara, Nārāyaṇa, Yama, Varuṇa, Kubera, the Four Great Heavenly Kings, Śrī-devī, Sarasvatī-devī, Hārītī-mātṛ, Śakunī-devī, Puṣpadantī-devī, and the five hundred sons of Hārītī.
They all sat together with their retinues and assemblies.
Furthermore, there were the Nāga King Sāgara, the Nāga King Nanda, and the Nāga King Upananda, surrounded by immeasurable hundreds of thousands of nāgas.

Furthermore, there were the Kinnara King and the Mahoraga King, surrounded before and behind by immeasurable retinues, who remained making great offerings while listening to the Dharma. Within that great assembly was a great Brahmin named Viṇḍu-datta.
He resided in the city of Pāṭaliputra.
This brahmin possessed vast wealth and treasures, so abundant that his great fortune rivaled that of Vaiśravaṇa, the Heavenly King.
This brahmin was learned, sagacious, wise, and discerning;
he had diligently cultivated virtuous qualities with pure faith and intention,
and had taken excellent refuge in the Triple Gem.
He was the foremost among the upāsakas.
That brahmin, having no offspring, pondered day and night:
"If I have no son, to what realm shall I be reborn?"
Furthermore, they have exterminated my clan. The Brahmin then reflected:
"The Great Teacher, the Buddha, the World-Honored One, is my father; I am the Buddha’s son."
The sublime Dharma is my mother; the noble Saṅgha is my brother.
Having met with great auspiciousness in this life, may I do so in future lives as well.
I now ask the Buddha, the World-Honored One:
by practicing what dharma-conduct do I gather together all roots of goodness through the cultivation of a single dharma?
Dedicating this toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment,
may the lineage of the Three Jewels be perpetually and eternally uninterrupted.
By virtue of these meritorious causes and conditions, may one obtain offspring.
"I now wish to ask the World-Honored One what dharmas and practices he cultivates.
At that time, the great Brahmin Viṇḍuḍāta went to where the World-Honored One was,
circumambulated the Buddha three times, and [stood before him].
With palms joined in reverence, he paid homage to the Buddha and addressed him, saying:
"World-Honored One, there is one dharma by which all roots of goodness are accumulated;
that is to say, the realization of unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
"Thus, may the roots of goodness shared with the Triple Gem become inexhaustible,
and may I obtain offspring.
The World-Honored One replied, "Excellent, excellent, Great Brahmin!"
Since you are able to inquire about such a meaning, listen now with great care and attention;
I shall now extensively praise and expound it for you.
O Great Brahmin, there is a Great King of Tantras, the Bodhimaṇḍālaṃkāra Dhāraṇī, by means of which [this is accomplished].
Planting all roots of goodness can fulfill all wishes.
I recall that in a past life,
outside the eastern gate of the city of Vārāṇasī.
There was a great park named Āśokavana.
Within it dwelt a rākṣasī.
Her name was Āśvalī. That rākṣasī was by nature violent and wrathful;
within a radius of a thousand yojanas, she [devoured] all the men and women.
Boys and girls were robbed of their vital essence.
The people within the city of Pāṭaliputra were constantly struck with terror and filled with great anxiety;
looking at one another, they all said, "What expedient means can we employ?"
Then the many elders addressed the multitude:
"Listen attentively! We have heard that a Buddha has appeared in the world;
that Buddha is named Wondrous Light Banner Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha."
"You all should go to that Buddha, the World-Honored One,
and ask the Buddha, the World-Honored One,
to rescue you from the perils of your grief and fear."
Then the multitude addressed the elders, saying,
"Where is the World-Honored One now?
The elders replied, "The World-Honored One is currently in the village of Vatsa."
This multitude of people spoke again to the elder,
saying, "By what means shall we act?
The elder replied, "Return to your homes."
In a clean place, one should prepare a square altar by smearing it with a mixture of cow dung and earth.
Make the four sides even and scatter various flowers upon them.
Place four incense burners, four vases of scented water, four sets of layered food offerings, and light four lamps.
Furthermore, take a *piṅgala* flask and fill it with scented water.
Place a tooth-stick upon the flask and should address that Tathāgata as follows:
I pray that the World-Honored One will deign to descend here at the time of the morning meal tomorrow.
The Tathāgata fully knows all matters of the past, future, and present.
The Tathāgata delivers all sentient beings who have fallen into the perilous realms.
May those in the hells, the hungry ghosts,
and the animal realm always be liberated;
at the time of the meal, the Tathāgata will surely descend with great supernormal powers.
Together with their retinues, they arrived at the city of Pāṭaliputra.
When the multitude of people heard these words,
they all assembled in a high, prominent, and pure location.
Mix cow dung with earth to smear upon the altar, and scatter various flowers over it.
Adorn the auspicious vase (bhadraghaṭa) and arrange various foods, drinks, unguents, and incense.
Then, lamps are placed in the four directions;
various musical instruments and golden *piṅgala* bird ornaments adorn jars filled with scented water,
upon which tooth-sticks are set.
Place it at the center of the maṇḍala and,
with a harmonious and elegant voice, chant aloud as follows:
"I prostrate and take refuge in the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Wondrous Light Banner."
I prostrate and take refuge in the Great Muni, the World-Honored One, who has compassion for all sentient beings.
I prostrate and take refuge in the Buddha, the World-Honored One, whose marvelous nature of reality is extraordinary.
I pray that you will deliver us, sentient beings who are undergoing suffering.
I pray that you will come tomorrow at mealtime to accept my offering,
to comfort us and all sentient beings,
and to serve as our refuge, our support, and our path to the happy realms.
"You have delivered us from this most terrifying, perilous, and difficult place.
As soon as this great assembly of beings had uttered these words,
the earth there shook in six ways.
A precious *kaṅkara* pitcher was overturned upon the ground,
whereupon it immediately became a great lotus pond,
filled with the wondrous eightfold meritorious waters of the devas.
The water is fragrant and pure, being neither cold nor hot, bringing delight to those who behold it.
Within the waters of that pond are various kinds of flowers;
namely, blue lotuses, red lotuses, pink lotuses, and white lotuses fill the interior of the pool.
The ground was strewn with golden sand and featured four jeweled stairways,
adorned with various interspersed precious gems;
his tooth-stick immediately transformed into a jewel-tree.
It is six yojanas in height and eight yojanas in length and breadth, being perfectly equal in all dimensions.
Its roots, trunks, branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits are all composed of the seven precious gems.
Furthermore, the ground in that place is vast, majestic, and pure.
Each side measures twelve yojanas, forming a great maṇḍala;
that place is delightful to the mind,
exquisitely beautiful, and most majestic.
Everywhere there were various kinds of flowers from both water and land.
Upon the flowering trees dwelt various birds— parrots, peacocks, kalaviṅkas, jīvañjīvakas, and other auspicious birds.
Their golden beaks and golden crests, and all their plumage, were composed of the seven treasures;
they emitted harmonious and elegant sounds.
That ground was adorned with various kinds of flowering trees.
That is to say: the tāmarasa trees, the campaka trees, the pāṭala trees, the aśoka trees,
the atimuktaka trees, and the sumana trees.
The kānana trees, śirīṣa trees, mahāśirīṣa trees, karkarava trees, and jhiṇṭikā trees.
The *yūthī*, *arka*, *śrīparṇī*, *nāgakesara*, and *vārṣika* trees, and so forth,
all exist because they are empowered by the spiritual power of the *dhāraṇī* for the adornment of the bodhimanda through the original vows of the Tathāgata Prabhāketu.
He performed a great supernatural manifestation.
At that time, the people of Pāṭaliputra were struck with wonder;
looking at one another, they said:
The manifestation of these great marks of supernormal power has appeared in accordance with what was previously required.
By whose power and by whose supernormal power has this great benefit and this great merit been manifested here in Jambudvīpa?
When these auspicious signs appeared in the world,
bringing great benefit to all sentient beings,
the multitude of people looked at one another and said:
"Each of you go and prepare various kinds of excellent food and drink;
tomorrow, invite the Buddha for a grand offering.
Then, that multitude of people each returned to their own homes.
That night, he prepared various kinds of food and drink, fragrant flowers, unguents, powdered incense, banners, streamers, and music.
Accompanied by a large retinue, he went halfway along the road to wait upon the World-Honored One.
At that time, the Tathāgata Prabhāketudhvaja was in the great village of Ardhalāṭa,
teaching the Dharma and transforming sentient beings within a great assembly.
Suddenly, before the assembly, there appeared a water flask made of the seven precious gems and a tooth-stick.
At that time, having seen this, the World-Honored One smiled and extended his golden arm, adorned with hundreds of thousands of merits;
he took the *piṅga* flask as well as the tooth-stick and remained in silent stillness.
At that time, when the great assembly had witnessed this event,
they all felt a sense of wonder and marveled at such an unprecedented occurrence;
seeing these auspicious signs, they did not yet know from which direction they should go to invite the World-Honored One.
At that time, there was among the assembly a bodhisattva mahāsattva named Subhūṣita-mati (妙清淨慧). He went to where the Buddha was,
prostrated himself with his head at the Buddha’s feet, and paid homage.
Having circumambulated him three times to the right, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, from whence does this auspicious sign come—
that the *piṅgala* water flask and the tooth-stick have appeared?"
He paid homage to the World-Honored One.
The Buddha said, "This *piṅgala* jar and tooth-stick have come from the great city of Pāṭaliputra.
He then addressed the Bodhisattva Subhūtinirmala:
"Those among you who wish to follow me may cast a tally;
by means of great supernatural power, we shall enter the great city of Pāṭaliputra tomorrow at dawn.
When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Subhūṣitamatī heard these words, he immediately cast a tally.
He addressed the assembly of śrāvakas and bodhisattvas: "Those among you who possess great supernormal powers and are able to perform the miracle of psychic travel may take this tally.
Tomorrow morning, we shall enter the city of Pāṭaliputra."
When the Bodhisattva Viśuddhamati had completed the distribution of the voting tallies,
he immediately requested the World-Honored One.
At that time, the World-Honored One, during the early morning hours, [proceeded].
With robes neatly arranged, accompanied by a great retinue and possessing majestic authority,
he exercised his supernatural powers through playful empowerment;
together with the great assembly, he immediately ascended into the void.
The devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas performed great music,
[offering] various kinds of incense, flowers, unguents, powdered incense, garments, and ornaments.
In the midst of the void,
he made offerings to the Tathāgata;
by means of the Buddha’s supernormal powers, he reached the great city of Pāṭaliputra in a mere instant.
Descending from the sky, they arrived at the site of the vast, majestic, and pure Great Maṇḍala and sat upon lion thrones.
Each member of that great assembly came to the gathering seated within their own respective emanated palaces.
At that time, by the Buddha's majestic spiritual power,

the multitude of people within the city each brought various kinds of offerings to the World-Honored One and the great assembly of bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, devas, nāgas, and the eight classes of beings.
The World-Honored One, knowing that the time for the meal was approaching,
had the assembly of śrāvakas all sit down to eat;
they ate to their heart's content, fully satisfied by various foods of diverse colors, fragrances, and exquisite flavors.
At that time, after the great assembly had finished eating,
they rinsed their mouths, washed their hands, and adjusted their robes; then,
by means of great supernormal powers, they again made offerings and circumambulated [the Buddha] three times.
Each sat down in order before the Buddha and reported the aforementioned matter to him, saying:
"World-Honored One, outside the eastern gate of this city..."
There is a garden named Āśokī.
In that garden dwells a rākṣasī named Puṣpāśokī.
His nature was violent and evil;
he constantly robbed boys and girls, both male and female, of their vital essence.
Day and night, he harbored a mind intent on harm.
"We only pray that the World-Honored One will reveal the skillful means to eliminate this calamity.
At that time, the Tathāgata Banner of Wondrous Light comforted the great assembly;
remaining in silent stillness, he manifested a smile.
From the Buddha’s face, various rays of light issued forth.

With this light, he illuminated the trichiliocosm, as well as the Aśokavana grove and the rākṣasī along with her hundreds of thousands of attendants; through the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, he caused that rākṣasī—
Together with their retinues, they fled in all four directions;
the garden was scorched like a single mass of fire as they wailed in grief and ran toward the ten quarters.
"To whom shall we return? Who will save us?
At that time, there were hosts of devas within the city who, from the air, uttered these words:
"You all should go to the presence of the Tathāgata Subhāṣitadhvaja, prostrate yourselves, and take refuge;
this shall cause you to obtain peace and happiness.
At that time, the rākṣasī Puṣpāsuri and her hundreds of thousands of attendants were filled with agitation.
He went to where the Buddha was, prostrated with his head at the Buddha's feet, and said to the Buddha: "I pray only that the World-Honored One will save me;
I pray only that the Bhagavān will save me."
"I only pray that the Sugata will save me.
World-Honored One, from this day forward, I shall never again dare to harm any sentient being, nor shall I ever again dare to oppress or afflict them.
At these words, the Tathāgata Wondrous Light Banner remained silent and granted his consent.
He immediately entered the samādhi called "Sporting with Supernatural Powers in the Field of Enlightenment through Empowerment. By entering this samādhi,
he illuminated all buddha-fields throughout the ten directions.
All the Tathāgatas within that land appeared clearly,
and he also heard the sounds of their voices as they preached the Dharma for the great assembly.
At that time, the Tathāgata Wondrous Light Banner...
He spoke the *Dhāraṇī of the Adornment of the Bodhimanda*.
All the Tathāgatas in the worlds of the ten directions praised him, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, O Tathāgata Wondrous Light Banner!"
This well-expounded King of Teachings, the Dharani for Adorning the Bodhimanda,
subdues the Rakshasi Pushpāśūri along with her retinue,
and establishes them in the ten paths of wholesome action.
He caused all the people to attain the stage of non-retrogression and established them upon the path of goodness; moreover,
the ground of that city was composed of the seven treasures.
And it rained down the seven precious jewels.
At that time, the people of Jambudvīpa were abundant, prosperous, and at peace.
O Great Brahmin, I was present during that period.
He was a young Brahmin boy,
seven years of age,
who heard this dhāraṇī.
Having conceived pure faith within the Buddha's teaching,
they shall realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
As for those great brahmins who may still harbor hesitation or doubt, [they too shall do so].
Was the rākṣasī Puṣpāśulī of former times anyone else?
She was none other than yourself. Why is this so, you rākṣasī Puṣpāśulī?
At that time, those who harm sentient beings and lack a heart of compassion will fall into the evil realms for immeasurable kalpas.
Great Brahmin, do not give rise to doubt.
At that time, the multitude of people within the city of Pāṭaliputra,
as well as these present devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, and kiṃnaras who have now gathered like clouds— [all were there].
At that time, this great brāhmaṇa may give rise to hesitation or doubt regarding those hundred thousand rākṣasī attendants.
One should not view it in such a way.
Why? Because within this assembly of mine are brahmins, kṣatriyas, brahmans, and nirgranthas.
This includes other non-Buddhist practitioners of frivolous discourse and illusory arts,
those who dwell in charnel grounds wearing rags and observing the cow-vow,
and those who dwell in mountain valleys observing ascetic precepts, and so forth.
At that time, after the Tathāgata Śākyamuni had finished speaking of these past causes and conditions,
he remained silent.
Then the entire great assembly...
Upon hearing these past causes and conditions,
everyone was struck with wonder and brought various kinds of incense, flowers, unguents, powdered incense, floral garlands, robes, banners, and streamers.
He went to where the World-Honored One was and made offerings;
circumambulating him three times to the right, he prostrated with his head at the Buddha's feet and spoke these words.
I only pray that the Blessed One will proclaim the King of Teachings, the Dharani for Adorning the Bodhimanda.
I only pray that the Blessed One will speak;
I only pray that the Sugata will speak this Great Vidyaraja.
May all sentient beings become great luminaries;
in the future final age, may all sentient beings be able to fulfill all their aspirations.
At that time, after the great assembly had made their request,
the World-Honored One remained silent for a while, then accepted the invitation with a smile.
Following this manifestation of his smile, he spoke.
From his face, various rays of light issued forth,
illuminating the worlds of the ten directions.
Having illuminated them, all the Buddhas within those worlds became fully manifest.
Furthermore, as soon as the words of the Dharma spoken by those Tathāgatas are heard,
seven-jeweled trees immediately arise within this ground;
the roots, trunks, branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits of these trees are most excellent.
The celestial, wondrous, and pleasing enjoyments and bliss manifest in Jambudvīpa;
that tree manifests great playful supernatural powers and blessings.
At that time, the youthful Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī,
having witnessed this supernatural power and seeing the Tathāgata’s smile,
approached the World-Honored One and prostrated himself at his feet.
Circumambulating the Buddha three times and joining his palms toward the Buddha, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, I pray that you will proclaim the King of Teachings, the Dhāraṇī for Adorning the Bodhimanda.
I pray that the Sugata will proclaim it."
To bring great benefit to all sentient beings and to nurture all who plant roots of virtue;
at that time, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni accepted the request of the youthful Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī.
He immediately entered the samādhi of contemplating the Buddha;
by the mere entry into this samādhi, in an instant, he—
He beheld all the Buddhas in the lands of the worlds of the ten directions as if they were within the range of a single arrow-shot;
those Buddhas of the worlds of the ten directions numbered ninety koṭis of hundreds of thousands of Ganges-sands.
They all assembled together and with one voice praised the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, Tathāgata Śākyamuni!
You have well expounded this great king of dhāraṇī teachings."
All Tathāgatas of the past have already spoken [of this],
and all have empowered it with their rejoicing.
We pray that the World-Honored One will extensively proclaim the ritual manual of the Great King of Teachings, the Dharani Method for Adorning the Bodhimanda.
At that time, the youthful Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī placed the Dharma-realm from which the Tathāgata was born into his alms bowl.
With both hands he held up the bowl and offered it to the Tathāgata.
At that time, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni extended his golden arm and accepted the bowl from the youthful Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī.
Having received them, he cast them into the air;
in an instant, his bowl filled the entirety of space with the relics of the Dharmadhātu and the images of the Tathāgatas contained therein.
Filling the void of the trichiliocosm,
those Tathāgatas all praised Śākyamuni Tathāgata, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, Śākyamuni Buddha!"
He saw before each and every Tathāgata a Śākyamuni Buddha together with his great assembly;
and before each and every Śākyamuni Buddha, [he likewise saw the same].
Furthermore, there was the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī,
who offered a bowl filled to the brim with the Dharma-realm,
manifesting great supernormal powers and great miraculous transformations.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi addressed the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, saying:
"How truly marvelous, O Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta!"
A miraculous manifestation is appearing within the great assembly of the Tathāgata.
For whom has this radiance and sign appeared?
By what causes and conditions, and by whose majestic power, has this great image of the Tathāgata and his assembly been manifested?
Mañjuśrī said, "Vajrapāṇi,
do you not know that this manifestation of light and miraculous transformation has appeared?
Vajrapāṇi replied:
Mañjuśrī, I have never before seen or heard of such a great assembly of all the Tathāgatas possessing such supernormal powers.
This rarity has never before been seen or heard.
Now I have finally been able to see it.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi whirled his vajra and circumambulated the World-Honored One to the right.
Standing before the Buddha, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, what Dharma do you wish to proclaim?
Now there appears a sign such as has never been seen or heard before."
Within the world, the signs of great supernormal power appeared clearly.
The Buddha said, "Vajrapāṇi, wait but a moment; you shall witness it for yourself.
In an instant, seven pillars made of the seven precious gems suddenly sprang forth from the earth before the Buddha, seven thousand yojanas in height and five thousand yojanas in width.
The celestial array was exquisitely adorned with a blazing radiance;
fine silken streamers and nets of pearls hung down, completely covering it above,
while tinkling bells moved to produce harmonious and elegant sounds, all further embellished by floral garlands.
Immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of devaputras descended from the sky,
holding various offering implements made of the seven precious jewels, and made offerings to the jeweled banner.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, saying:
"You may go and open the Banner Gate.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi’s entire body was ablaze with flames, as fiercely radiant as a mass of fire.
Adorned with a crown and necklaces, his body was resplendent;
grasping a vajra, his face was wrathful and struck terror into all who beheld him.
Approaching the precious banner, he extended his right arm and opened the gate of the banner.
Having opened the gate of the banner,
there was within that banner a lion throne made of Jambūnada gold.
Adorned with the seven precious jewels,
various kinds of exquisite celestial garments were spread upon his seat.
There sat the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, King of Vast and Expansive Countenance, Golden Mouth, Sublime and Valiant Radiance Banner Peak.
Sitting upon it, he entered samādhi and appeared.
At that time, the Tathāgata Vipulakāñcanamukha-unnatavikrama-prabhāketu praised Śākyamuni Buddha, saying:
Excellent, excellent, Śākyamuni Tathāgata!
You manifest great supernormal transformations within the world and manifest the great assembly of Tathāgatas.
There has never been a gathering of miraculous transformations equal to this.
Even among the previous Buddhas who attained perfect enlightenment, there has never before been such a display of supernatural powers by a Tathāgata in an assembly.
We pray only that the Blessed One will proclaim this *Dhāraṇī-śāstra-rāja*, the Adornment of the Bodhimanda.
For the benefit, happiness, and compassion of many beings,
this assembly of the Tathāgata’s image, manifesting through miraculous powers,
displays this banner-sign.
All of this is due to the power of the *dhāraṇī* that adorns the site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*).
These miraculous transformations have been manifested,
and these omens were first displayed through the empowerment (*adhiṣṭhāna*) of this very *dhāraṇī*.
"I only pray that the World-Honored One will preach the Great King of Teachings,
the Dharani of the Adornment of the Bodhimanda. Then, the Tathagata Śākyamuni,
having received the request of the Tathagata Vipulavaktra-suvarṇa-mukha-ucca-vīra-prabhā-ketu-cūḍa, [consented].

Place four vases of fragrant water at the four corners.
Use four vessels to hold food and drink as offerings, and place four incense burners at the four gates.
In addition, provide various kinds of food and drink, diverse flower garlands, and the "three white foods.
Place four lamps at the four corners.
The practitioner shall sit facing east.
During the latter part of the night, one should enter the maṇḍala to protect the body and bind the boundaries.
As soon as one enters this maṇḍala,
all karmic obstacles and hindrances are completely extinguished.
All siddhis shall be accomplished;
all accumulations of merit shall grow and increase;
one shall attain the Bodhi of the Buddha and remain far removed from all evil destinies.
They shall not be harassed by any ghosts or spirits;
all the devas will provide protection, so that they always enjoy peace and security day and night,
and together with their companions, they shall obtain great guardianship.
By entering this maṇḍala, one attains the stage of non-retrogression.
I shall now recite the heart-dhāraṇī:
Oṃ sarvatathāgatavyavalokite jaya jaya svāhā. The heart-of-the-heart dhāraṇī is as follows: [recitation].
Oṃ hulu hulu jaye mukhe svāhā. This is the dhāraṇī for bathing and purification.
Oṃ jvalini jvāle svāhā. This is the dhāraṇī for binding the boundary. Oṃ samantapracaṇḍe jaye svāhā.
The Dharani for Binding the Mandala Boundary: Oṃ maṇḍalajāye svāhā.
The Dharani for Offering Food: Oṃ śrī-maṇḍalajāye svāhā. The Dharani for Invitation: Oṃ sarvasandhare maṇḍalajāye svāhā.
The Dharani for Offering Flowers: Oṃ buddhaguṇe svāhā. The Dharani for Offering Incense: Oṃ jaya-gandhe svāhā.
The Dharani for Consecration: Oṃ vijaya-kṣve svāhā. Tie the topknot.
Dhāraṇī: Oṃ tathāgatajaye svāhā. Dhāraṇī for consecrating robes: Oṃ jayavṛtte svāhā.
Dhāraṇī for protecting the disciple’s body: Oṃ kuraḍari svāhā.
Dhāraṇī for Invoking and Escorting the Holy Assembly: Oṃ dhara dhara mīrajaye svāhā. Dhāraṇī for Consecrating the Rosary:
Oṃ susambhavajaye svāhā. Dhāraṇī for Offering the Seat: Oṃ sunarījaye svāhā.
Hā va-vinayaka-dhāraṇī: Oṃ suriyaye svāhā. Dhāraṇī for Invoking All Tathāgatas: Oṃ pravarājya-siddhe svāhā. Dhāraṇī for Protecting the Body: Oṃ rakṣa.
*Nirjaye svāhā*—the mantra for offering lamps. *Oṃ jaya nibhini svāhā*—the mantra for *homa*.
*Oṃ māre vimāra-jaye svāhā*—the mantra for inviting all Tathāgatas. *Oṃ sarasa*...
*Varajaye siddhi svāhā*. I shall now explain the function of the Heart Mantra and the Heart-of-the-Heart Mantra for the practice of cultivation.
If one recites the heart-dhāraṇī one hundred thousand times, one will attain the status of a vidyādhara;
as for the khaṭvāṅga, take realgar and place it within a vessel of refined copper.
If one applies [this substance] to the forehead after reciting the mantra one thousand times,
one will immediately attain the power to soar through the void.
All the palace gates of the devas, nāgas, and the eight classes of supernatural beings will open, allowing one to see within them.
One will attain the power to enter and roam at will,
with a lifespan of one kalpa.
Furthermore, if one consecrates the *saptalā* eye-salve one hundred thousand times and applies it to the eyes, [the same result is achieved].
One will immediately obtain the *antaḥpura* [seal].
All the palaces of the ghosts and spirits will open, and one shall be able to enter them.
Furthermore, according to another method, one should recite it ten thousand times.
One will behold all Tathāgatas.
Furthermore, by consecrating a stūpa pillar eight thousand times with this dharma,
it should be placed atop the stūpa.
When the relics of all Tathāgatas enter this stūpa, it becomes a great śarīra-stūpa.
Furthermore, there is a method: take the bowl of Mañjuśrī.
He empowered the alms bowl eight thousand times,
filled it with milk-rice porridge, placed it in the hand of Mañjuśrī,
and then requested [the food] from the Bodhisattva.
A thousand people could not finish eating this porridge.
Furthermore, there is another method: take the mantras from other sections and empower them with this dhāraṇī.
Whatever one desires, it will be accomplished as soon as it is performed.
I shall now explain the method of the mudrā:
extend both hands flatly.
Place the right hand over the left,
with palms facing upward and resting upon the heart;
this is called the Root Seal of the Bodhimaṇḍālaṃkāra Dhāraṇī.
As soon as this mudrā is bound, all sins are extinguished;
all Tathāgatas comfort that person,
and it also accomplishes the invocation of all Tathāgatas.
If one forms this mudrā, all Tathāgatas will show the highest respect for that person.
This is the original root mudrā; raise the right hand, and it may be employed in all circumstances.
This immediately constitutes all mudrās and is empowered by all Tathāgatas;
place the right hand below the navel.
Press the tip of the thumb against the tip of the index finger.
This mudrā is common to all mudrās and is empowered by all Tathāgatas.
By binding this mudrā, one is freed from all sinful obstructions.
At that time, Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva spoke a dhāraṇī;
for the purpose of protecting and upholding the teaching of this dhāraṇī, the dhāraṇī is as follows:

*Namo Mañjuśriye Kumārabhūtāya tadyathā | Jaye vijaye jaye śrī-ṛddhi hūṃ svāhā.* When reciting this, whether at the beginning of the preliminary practices or when seeking spiritual accomplishment (*siddhi*).
First, recite this dhāraṇī seven times;
then one will be free from obstacles and swiftly attain accomplishment.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, the Lord of Secrets, spoke.
He spoke this great vidyā-dhāraṇī, saying:
*Tadyathā | vajramuṣṭi-hanana-hābha-cavajra hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*. By means of this dhāraṇī...
Consecrate white mustard seeds seven times;
scatter them in the four directions at the site of recitation,
and a great boundary will be established immediately.
At that time, the Four Great Heavenly Kings spoke this mantra:
*Tadyathā dṛṣṭi hiri miri saraprasara bili bili svāhā*. With this mantra, one should empower white mustard seeds and water twenty-one times.
As it was poured over his crown,
all the ghosts, spirits, and yakṣas were completely subdued;
they prostrated at his feet in reverence and withdrew.
At that time, when the World-Honored One had finished speaking this sutra,
the youthful Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi the Great Lord of Secrets, and the Four Great Heavenly Kings [arose from their seats].
Together with all the devas, nāgas, the eight classes of beings, humans, and non-humans,
having heard what the Buddha had spoken, they were all greatly rejoiced, believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
*The Dhāraṇī Sūtra on the Adornments of the Bodhimaṇḍa*.
